name: Canada
hook: The world's second-largest country, asked through its provinces, capitals and oil.

facts.label: the second-largest country
facts.statement: Canada is the largest country in the Commonwealth by area and the only mainland country in the Western Hemisphere bordering just one country.

facts.label: Newfoundland and British Columbia
facts.statement: Newfoundland, long called Terra Nova, is Canada's newest province; British Columbia joined in 1871, giving Canada both Atlantic and Pacific coasts.

facts.label: Quebec
facts.statement: Quebec is the French-speaking province north of Vermont; its namesake city fell to the British in 1759.

facts.label: Ottawa
facts.statement: Ottawa was chosen as Canada's capital in 1857; it is the country's fourth-largest city and home to the National Gallery.

facts.label: Toronto
facts.statement: Toronto, once named York, is Canada's largest city; its 1,815-foot CN Tower is the world's tallest self-supporting structure.

facts.label: the Prairie provinces
facts.statement: The 1947 Leduc oil strike set off Alberta's oil boom; Manitoba is the only Prairie province that is not landlocked.

facts.label: Prince Edward Island
facts.statement: Prince Edward Island is Canada's smallest province and the only one separated entirely from the North American mainland.
